title: slab-compaction-and-kv-slice-sizing-tune-for-llama-mistral-qwen-longctx
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce GPU fragmentation and peak memory for long-context workloads (>32k tokens) across high-memory variants (Llama-2-70B, Mistral-8x-large, Qwen-2-32k) by introducing a slab compaction pass and variant-aware KV slice sizing. The compaction pass should run opportunistically during low-throughput windows and avoid stalling the main token generation path. We will tune default KV slice sizes per-model-variant and provide runtime knobs to override for Dedicated/private customers.
background: We observe 12-22% extra peak GPU memory due to KV slab fragmentation under mixed batch sizes with our continuous batching flow. Qwen-2-32k shows worst-case 22% overhead on A100-40GB with long prefix reuse; Llama-2-70B shows ~15% overhead. Current eviction heuristics target LRU across whole KV; they don't account for per-variant residency patterns (e.g., Mistral has shorter active KV windows). This task is a targeted optimizer: compact partially-free slabs, tighten slice granularity for large-embedding heads, and adjust eviction thresholds for quantized variants.
proposed_changes: 1) Add an async slab-compaction thread that coalesces small free spans into larger contiguous spans when GPU utilization < 40%. 2) Introduce per-variant KV slice templates (small/medium/large) instead of a one-size fits all; default templates: Llama-2-70B -> large-slice, Mistral-8x -> medium-slice, Qwen-2-32k -> extra-large-slice. 3) Change eviction policy to preference: stale-prefix-age + soft residency cap; evict fractional oldest slices rather than whole KV segments. 4) Expose runtime flags: --kv-compaction-frequency, --kv-slice-template, --kv-evict-threshold.
benchmarks_and_results: Local perf runs on a5.xlarge simulate long-prompts with mixed batch sizes (1/4/8). Baseline peak memory: Qwen-2-32k = 39.8GB (A100-40), Llama-2-70B = 62.3GB (A100-80 emulated). After prototype compaction + variant templates: Qwen peak = 31.2GB (-21.6%), Llama peak = 54.9GB (-11.8%). 99th-pct latency change: +2.3ms on small batches, -1.1ms on 8-batch due to denser placement. Throughput unchanged or improved under high concurrency. Note: quantized 4-bit variants showed slightly higher eviction churn; tuned residency cap improved stability.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Compaction on busy hosts may increase tail latency if not gated correctly; mitigate with strict GPU utilization checks. - Variant templates add operational surface area; wrong template could increase swaps. - Async compaction requires careful synchronization to avoid KV corruption during slice re-mapping. - Edge cases for private on-prem with strict jitter budgets require per-customer opt-out.
tasks: Design compaction algorithm and safety checks (lockless re-map plan)
Implement async compaction thread and GPU utilization probe
Add per-variant KV slice templates and config plumbing
Modify eviction policy to support fractional-slice eviction
Unit tests for slab invariants + fuzz test KV remap under concurrent read/write
Integration tests with continuous batching harness (simulate mixed batches)
Performance runs across Llama/Mistral/Qwen on A100 and H100 profiles
Docs: runtime flags, recommended templates, troubleshooting guide
Create rollout plan: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global with automatic rollback
acceptance_criteria: Peak GPU memory reduced >= 10% for Llama/Mistral/Qwen long-context baselines in our perf harness
No >5% regression in 99th-pct latency for small-batch (<=2) under normal load
Compaction does not cause KV corruption (zero data loss) across fuzz tests
Runtime flags documented and tested in Dedicated/private install scripts
Automated CI checks added to prevent regressions on eviction logic
